meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?

Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.
I forgot the keys.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'являть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to declare'.

examples.trans: I am reporting it stolen.
Will you report to the police?
I will not report it.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Is this our car now?
Which car did you come in?
A car. A German one.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'load, burden'.

examples.trans: Keep your weight off that leg.

examples.text: Врач сказал пока сильно не нагружать больную ногу.
examples.trans: The doctor said not to put much weight on the injured leg for now.

examples.text: Не надо нагружать нового повара всеми заказами сразу.
examples.trans: Do not overload the new cook with all the orders at once.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'strain, anguish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You have a partial ligament tear.

examples.text: Врач сказал, что у вас небольшой надрыв связок.
examples.trans: The doctor said that you have a slight ligament tear.

examples.text: Она говорила об этом с настоящим душевным надрывом.
examples.trans: She spoke about it with real emotional anguish.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ехать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'confront, run into'.

examples.trans: And it ran over me.

examples.text: Водитель не заметил знак и случайно наехал на бордюр.
examples.trans: The driver did not notice the sign and accidentally ran into the curb.

examples.text: Почему шеф с самого утра так строго наехал на нас?
examples.trans: Why did the chef come down so hard on us first thing in the morning?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.

No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Russian uses one word for both. Common feminine noun meaning 'leg, foot' in everyday Russian.
Russian uses one word for both. Common feminine noun meaning 'leg, foot' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The right foot.
My leg hurts.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + instrumental (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'under' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Used in the singular. Borrowed in the Petrine era from German 'Polizei' / French 'police' (from Greek 'politeia', civil administration).

examples.trans: Call the police!

examples.text: Тут кнопки вызова: скорая, полиция и мы.
examples.trans: Here are the call buttons: ambulance, police, and us.

meanings.note: + в: попасть в цель. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пасть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hit; to get (somewhere)', paired with 'попадать'.

meanings.en: to get to, to end up
meanings.note: как попасть в центр? = how do I get to the centre?

examples.trans: Say a firework hit the power station. Three districts without electricity.

meanings.note: Поставить защёлку = fit a latch. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to place (upright)', paired with 'ставить'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to place (upright)', paired with 'ставить'.

meanings.note: Causing fear or feeling frightened. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I got scared.
